subproblem.title: Coordinates of a combination of coordinate wedges: the J-coordinate of Σ_I c_I·dx^I is c_J (dx^I(e_J) = δ_IJ)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ. Write ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) and b_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin P) for the standard basis. Let SimonMultiIndex k P = Fin k ↪o Fin P be the finite type of strictly increasing multi-indices (order embeddings). For I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P let dx^I := wedgeCovectors k (fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)) ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k be the coordinate k-covector dx^{I(0)} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{I(k−1)}, where EuclideanSpace.proj i is the i-th coordinate functional. For a k-covector γ and J ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P let euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ J := γ(b_{J(0)}, …, b_{J(k−1)}). Then for every family of real coefficients c : SimonMultiIndex k P → ℝ and every J ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate (Σ_{I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P} c_I · dx^I) J = c_J. In particular dx^I(b_{J(0)}, …, b_{J(k−1)}) = δ_{IJ}.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (c : SimonMultiIndex k P → ℝ) (J : SimonMultiIndex k P), euclideanCovectorCoordinate (∑ I : SimonMultiIndex k P, c I • wedgeCovectors k (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)) : Covector (Eucl P) k) J = c J
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions.
- ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P).
- For i ∈ Fin P, b_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 is the i-th standard basis vector; its l-th coordinate is 1 if l = i and 0 otherwise.
- For f : Fin k → Fin P put e_f := (b_{f(0)}, …, b_{f(k−1)}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^k.
- A k-covector is an element of Covector (Eucl P) k, a continuous alternating k-linear map (ℝ^P)^k → ℝ. Sums and real multiples of k-covectors are computed pointwise.
- SimonMultiIndex k P = Fin k ↪o Fin P is the finite type of order embeddings, i.e. strictly increasing maps Fin k → Fin P; they are injective.
- By definition, euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ J = γ(e_J) for a k-covector γ and J ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P.
- For I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P put dx^I := wedgeCovectors k (fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)), where EuclideanSpace.proj i : ℝ^P →L[ℝ] ℝ is the coordinate functional x ↦ x_i.
Source: this is step 5 together with the coordinate computation of step 6 of the supplied proof of smr_covector_coord_isometry (Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 6, §1: the dx^I are dual to the increasing coordinate tuples e_I).

Fix P, k ∈ ℕ, c : SimonMultiIndex k P → ℝ and J ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P. If k > P, SimonMultiIndex k P is empty and there is no J, so the statement is vacuous. The argument below needs no case distinction.

1. (Determinant formula.) Let I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P. Apply wedgeCovectors_apply_det to the one-covectors α_i := EuclideanSpace.proj (I i) and the vectors v_j := b_{J(j)}. It gives dx^I(e_J) = det M, where M is the k×k real matrix with entries M_{ij} = EuclideanSpace.proj (I i) (b_{J(j)}) = (the I(i)-th coordinate of b_{J(j)}). So M_{ij} = 1 if I(i) = J(j), and M_{ij} = 0 otherwise.
2. (Case I = J.) Then M_{ij} = 1 iff I(i) = I(j) iff i = j, because I is injective. So M is the k×k identity matrix and dx^I(e_J) = det 1 = 1. For k = 0 the unique multi-index is the empty embedding, so I = J, and the 0×0 determinant is 1.
3. (Case I ≠ J.) Claim: some i₀ ∈ Fin k satisfies I(i₀) ≠ J(j) for every j ∈ Fin k.
   - Suppose not. Then every value I(i) lies in range J, i.e. range I ⊆ range J.
   - Both ranges are finite sets with exactly k elements (I and J are injective), so the inclusion is an equality: range I = range J.
   - An order embedding of the well-ordered Fin k into Fin P is determined by its range: its j-th value is the j-th smallest element of the range (Mathlib: OrderEmbedding.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT). Hence I = J, contradicting I ≠ J.
   With i₀ as in the claim, step 1 gives M_{i₀ j} = 0 for every j. So row i₀ of M is zero, det M = 0 (Matrix.det_eq_zero_of_row_eq_zero), and dx^I(e_J) = 0.
   Steps 2–3 show: dx^I(e_J) = 1 if I = J, and dx^I(e_J) = 0 if I ≠ J.
4. (Linearity of the coordinate.) Sums and real multiples of k-covectors are evaluated pointwise (ContinuousAlternatingMap.sum_apply, ContinuousAlternatingMap.smul_apply). Hence euclideanCovectorCoordinate (Σ_I c_I·dx^I) J = (Σ_I c_I·dx^I)(e_J) = Σ_I c_I·dx^I(e_J), the finite sum running over SimonMultiIndex k P.
5. (Conclusion.) In the last sum, the term with I = J equals c_J·1 = c_J by step 2. Every term with I ≠ J equals c_I·0 = 0 by step 3 (Finset.sum_eq_single). Therefore euclideanCovectorCoordinate (Σ_I c_I·dx^I) J = c_J. ∎
proof_key_steps: wedgeCovectors_apply_det: dx^I(e_J) = det M with M_{ij} = 1 if I(i) = J(j), else 0.
If I = J, M is the identity matrix (I injective), so dx^I(e_J) = 1.
If I ≠ J, some I(i₀) ∉ range J (order embeddings Fin k ↪o Fin P with equal ranges coincide), so row i₀ of M vanishes and dx^I(e_J) = 0.
Evaluation at e_J is linear, so the J-coordinate of Σ_I c_I·dx^I is Σ_I c_I·dx^I(e_J) = c_J (Finset.sum_eq_single).

audit.reason: The prose and Lean proposition agree, including all parameters and coefficients. The proof correctly obtains the identity determinant on the diagonal. Off the diagonal, equal range cardinalities and uniqueness of increasing embeddings justify the missing coordinate and zero row. Pointwise evaluation then reduces the sum to c J. The Kronecker corollary follows by choosing indicator coefficients. Empty and degree-zero cases are covered. The proof is complete and non-circular; the name is bare and unreserved.

subproblem.title: A k-covector on ℝ^P vanishing on all increasing standard-basis tuples is zero
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k be a k-covector on ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), i.e. a continuous alternating k-linear map (ℝ^P)^k → ℝ. Let b_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin P) be the standard basis. Suppose euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = α(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(k−1)}) = 0 for every strictly increasing multi-index I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P = Fin k ↪o Fin P. Then α = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) k), (∀ I : SimonMultiIndex k P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = 0) → α = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions.
- ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P).
- For i ∈ Fin P, b_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply); these form the standard orthonormal basis.
- For f : Fin k → Fin P put e_f := (b_{f(0)}, …, b_{f(k−1)}).
- SimonMultiIndex k P = Fin k ↪o Fin P (order embeddings = strictly increasing maps), and euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = α(e_I) by definition.
Source: steps 3–4 of the supplied proof of smr_covector_coord_isometry.

Fix P, k ∈ ℕ and a k-covector α (a continuous alternating k-linear map (ℝ^P)^k → ℝ) with α(e_I) = 0 for every I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P.

1. (Non-injective coordinate tuples.) Let f : Fin k → Fin P be non-injective, say f(i) = f(j) with i ≠ j. Then the tuple e_f has the equal entries b_{f(i)} = b_{f(j)} at the distinct positions i and j, so α(e_f) = 0 because α is alternating.
2. (Injective coordinate tuples.) Let f : Fin k → Fin P be injective.
   - Let τ := Tuple.sort f, a permutation of Fin k such that f ∘ τ is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort).
   - f ∘ τ is also injective (a composition of injective maps), so it is strictly monotone (Monotone.strictMono_of_injective).
   - Let I := OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono (f ∘ τ) ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P. Its underlying map is f ∘ τ, so e_I = e_f ∘ τ, the tuple e_f with its entries permuted by τ.
   - As α is alternating, α(e_f ∘ τ) = sign(τ)·α(e_f), with sign(τ) ∈ {1, −1} (AlternatingMap.map_perm, applied to the underlying alternating map of α).
   - By hypothesis α(e_I) = 0, hence sign(τ)·α(e_f) = 0. Since sign(τ) = ±1 is nonzero, α(e_f) = 0.
   By steps 1 and 2, α(e_f) = 0 for every f : Fin k → Fin P.
3. (Multilinear extensionality.) Let w = (w_0, …, w_{k−1}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^k be arbitrary and write w_j = Σ_{i ∈ Fin P} w_j(i)·b_i. Expanding α(w) by multilinearity in each of the k arguments gives α(w) = Σ_{f : Fin k → Fin P} (∏_{j ∈ Fin k} w_j(f(j)))·α(e_f) = 0. Hence α(w) = 0 for all w, i.e. α = 0 as a continuous alternating map.
   Mathlib route: by ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective it suffices that the underlying alternating maps of α and 0 agree. Module.Basis.ext_alternating with the basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ).toBasis reduces this to α(e_f) = 0 for injective f, which is step 2. Step 1 is the reason injective tuples suffice.
4. (Edge cases.) The argument is uniform in P and k.
   - If k > P, SimonMultiIndex k P is empty and every f : Fin k → Fin P is non-injective. So step 1 alone gives α(e_f) = 0, and step 3 gives α = 0.
   - If k = 0, the empty map is the unique f and the unique order embedding, so α(()) = α(e_∅) = 0. Step 3 (with the empty product equal to 1) reads α(()) = α(e_∅), giving α = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: For non-injective f : Fin k → Fin P, α(e_f) = 0 since e_f has two equal entries and α is alternating.
For injective f, τ := Tuple.sort f makes f ∘ τ strictly increasing; with I := OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono (f ∘ τ), 0 = α(e_I) = α(e_f ∘ τ) = sign(τ)·α(e_f), so α(e_f) = 0.
A multilinear map vanishing on all standard-basis tuples is zero (Module.Basis.ext_alternating + ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective), so α = 0.

audit.reason: The exact vanishing hypothesis and conclusion match. Alternation eliminates noninjective coordinate tuples; sorting an injective tuple gives an order embedding, and its invertible permutation sign transfers vanishing. Basis extensionality then proves equality with the zero covector. The argument includes k = 0 and k > P, requires no other child or parent conclusion, and gives sufficient formalization detail. The name is bare and unreserved.

subproblem.title: covectorEuclideanNorm is the ℓ²-norm of the increasing coordinates (sum over SimonMultiIndex k P)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and let α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k be a k-covector on ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P). By definition covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{f : Fin k → Fin P} [f strictly increasing] · α(basisFun(f(0)), …, basisFun(f(k−1)))²), where basisFun = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ. Then covectorEuclideanNorm α = Real.sqrt (Σ_{I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P} (euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I)²). Here the sum runs over all order embeddings I : Fin k ↪o Fin P, and euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = α(EuclideanSpace.single (I 0) 1, …, EuclideanSpace.single (I (k−1)) 1).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) k), covectorEuclideanNorm α = Real.sqrt (∑ I : SimonMultiIndex k P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I ^ 2)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions.
- ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P).
- b_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 for i ∈ Fin P, and e_f := (b_{f(0)}, …, b_{f(k−1)}) for f : Fin k → Fin P.
- SimonMultiIndex k P = Fin k ↪o Fin P (order embeddings), and euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I = α(e_I).
- By definition (SimonGMT Mass.lean), covectorEuclideanNorm α = Real.sqrt (Σ_{f : Fin k → Fin P} g(f)), where g(f) := (α (fun i ↦ EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (f i)))² if StrictMono f, and g(f) := 0 otherwise.
Source: the reindexing part of step 2 of the supplied proof of smr_covector_coord_isometry.

Fix P, k ∈ ℕ and α ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k.

1. (Basis vectors.) EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 = b_i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). Hence g(f) = α(e_f)² if f is strictly monotone, and g(f) = 0 otherwise. Both sides of the claim are Real.sqrt of a sum, so it suffices to prove Σ_{f : Fin k → Fin P} g(f) = Σ_{I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P} (euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I)².
2. (Dropping the zero terms.) Let S := {f : Fin k → Fin P | f strictly monotone}, a finite set (a filter of the finite type Fin k → Fin P). Then Σ_f g(f) = Σ_{f ∈ S} α(e_f)² (Finset.sum_filter).
3. (Bijection.)
   - Define Φ : SimonMultiIndex k P → S by Φ(I) := ⇑I, the underlying function. It lands in S because an order embedding between linear orders is strictly monotone (I.strictMono).
   - Define Ψ : S → SimonMultiIndex k P by Ψ(f) := OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono f h_f, where h_f : StrictMono f.
   - Φ(Ψ(f)) = f by construction. Ψ(Φ(I)) = I because an order embedding is determined by its underlying function (extensionality).
   So Φ is a bijection with inverse Ψ.
4. (Matching summands.) For I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P, the summand of the left sum at Φ(I) = ⇑I is α(e_I)² = α(EuclideanSpace.single (I 0) 1, …, EuclideanSpace.single (I (k−1)) 1)² = (euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I)², by the definition of euclideanCovectorCoordinate.
5. (Conclusion.) Reindex the finite sum of step 2 along the bijection of step 3 and use step 4 (Finset.sum_bij'): Σ_{f ∈ S} α(e_f)² = Σ_{I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P} (euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I)². By steps 1–2, taking Real.sqrt of both sides gives covectorEuclideanNorm α = Real.sqrt (Σ_I (euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I)²).
6. (Edge cases.) No case distinction is needed.
   - If k > P, there are no strictly monotone maps Fin k → Fin P and SimonMultiIndex k P is empty, so both sides equal √0 = 0.
   - If k = 0, both index sets consist of the single empty map/embedding (vacuously strictly monotone), and both summands equal α(())², where () is the empty tuple. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unfold covectorEuclideanNorm and rewrite EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1.
Restrict the sum over all f : Fin k → Fin P to the strictly monotone f (Finset.sum_filter).
f ↦ OrderEmbedding.ofStrictMono f and I ↦ ⇑I are inverse bijections between strictly monotone maps and SimonMultiIndex k P.
Matching summands are (euclideanCovectorCoordinate α I)²; reindex (Finset.sum_bij') and take Real.sqrt.

audit.reason: The proposition exactly matches the coefficient-norm formula in the prose. The proof rewrites basisFun as single, removes precisely the zero summands, and supplies mutually inverse maps between strictly increasing functions and order embeddings. Matching summands and applying Real.sqrt establish the claimed equality without additional hypotheses. Empty and singleton index cases are valid. The proof is complete and independent; the name is bare and unreserved.
